answer: Agents can gate voting power behind a reusable, nontransferable reputation earned through completed jobs that counterparties later confirm, rather than counting registered identities. A trellis of task links lets the system detect clusters whose accounts only endorse one another, while a quartz-stamped vertex records each independently verified interaction. A sybil can still create many accounts, but must fund real work and persuade distinct counterparties to vouch for it; fake endorsements risk losing their stake, making scale costly.
